This is one of those rare videos where the takeaway is a framework, not just a stock list. 
 
The part that impressed me most was how you built the QARP process layer by layer—starting with defining quality through ROE, ROCE, debt, cash flow and earnings quality, then contrasting it with GARP, and finally adding the four practical checks: *why* the price has fallen, competitive advantage, promoter quality, and EPS + valuation. Even the point where you corrected your own 15% sales growth filter and explained why it was drifting toward GARP instead of QARP added a lot of credibility. 
 
One question I'd genuinely love your perspective on: When a company scores well on quantitative quality metrics but its moat is changing due to regulation or new competition (like the IEX example), what qualitative signals do you track first to decide whether it's a temporary value compression or the beginning of structural decline? 
 
This is the kind of content that genuinely changes how someone evaluates businesses, not just what they buy.

So nice of you. Thank you so much 🙌 

You are right. Quantitative metrics often miss out on experience/quality narrations. I've explained a few in my earlier videos:
a) Just Dial -- the cash-rich value trap .. https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=jWB0N_m2DF4
b) Dreamfolks and the Adani challenge .. https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=fAQ-yazjVq0
c) IEX and the impact of regulation .. https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=yw5OHVQVtvI
d) Kamat Hotels and delays in execution .. https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=f5kuy3f6V2E
e) Impact of commodity/RM price on sales growth .. https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=7dyDJWAzdhQ
Since my frustrations/learnings were plenty so I put all of it together in this video -- https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=UzvmdiQu4U8

With re: your question, let me take an example. Kalyan Jewellers stock price fell by almost 30% between April & Jun 2026. There was no real reason for this fall in terms of news. Only some conjecture on lower sales growth, import duty or similar things. But the sales growth was still strong (45-60% YOY) and a normalized 25% seemed a few more quarters away. Secondly, the PE ratio of Kalyan was at 25 in early June -- which is remarkable for India's second biggest gold jewellery retailer when the biggest (Titan) is at a multiple of 70. And finally, structurally India is moving towards formal sale of jewellery and is expected to be like this for a few more years. Net net, I looked at the price drop as a temporary compression in value rather than a structural decline -- and invested in that stock

Hello Dinesh ji, thank you for your support & kind words

I don't share my portfolio/trades as it brings with it a lot of stress. While most people are forgiving and don't expect 100% success rate from me ..  there are still many who lack the ability & patience to navigate certain situations. While there's a plus side (additional income) but I feel the cost of it is too high --- a) high levels of anxiety, b) explaining myself, c) glued to investing screen, d) inability to take breaks/vacations etc.

I do the best when I work on my preferred pace, with no stress and flexibility. I believe it's also why my videos come out well & gel with many viewers. It's my job to protect it -- and I plan to

With re: workshops -- yes, I would like that. I will certainly have something in the next 4-5 months. First peek -- I want to a series of classes (8-10) on stock picking. It's not just classes, I would also do some handholding so that learner can be confident of picking stocks & navigating the market incl. selling & behaviour. After many years of refining my approach & making mistakes, I am now a lot more confident of my stock picking skills. I'll keep everyone updated on the classes via Youtube
